speaker: Doctor
text: I am Dr. Agent. Please describe your neck and arm pain, including where it starts, where it radiates, and how long you have had these symptoms. To help me assess your muscle weakness and paresthesias, could you tell me specifically which muscles are weak and what type of numbness you are feeling?

speaker: Patient
text: 58-year-old male. The patient reports a year-long history of burning pain in his neck and arms, accompanying paresthesias in his hands. Over the past 3 months, he has experienced increasing weakness in both hands. He has a history of type 2 diabetes mellitus, hypercholesterolemia, and hypertension. He was involved in a motor vehicle accident 3 years ago.

speaker: Doctor
text: Thank you. Given your burning pain, paresthesias, and progressive hand weakness, I need to clarify if this weakness is symmetric in both hands or worse on one side, and whether you experience difficulty with fine motor tasks like buttoning shirts. Also, do you have any numbness in your groin or buttocks, and have you noticed any changes in your bladder or bowel control?

speaker: Patient
text: My main symptom is Burning pain in neck and arms, and weakness in both hands. I also have Paresthesias in hands, Absent reflexes, Decreased hand grip with fasciculations.

speaker: Doctor
text:
DIAGNOSIS READY: Amyotrophic Lateral Sclerosis (ALS)

The combination of progressive bilateral hand weakness, fasciculations, and absent reflexes is highly specific. I am requesting nerve conduction studies and EMG to confirm the diagnosis. REQUEST TEST: Nerve_Conduction_Study; EMG. REQUEST IMAGES: MRI_Cervical_Spine.
